sections.text: # Late Wittgenstein: Language Games and Meaning as Use

metadata.title: Late Wittgenstein: Language Games and Meaning as Use
Late Wittgenstein: Language Games and Meaning as Use

sections.text: Ludwig Wittgenstein returned to philosophy at Cambridge in 1929 after nearly a decade away. Over the following decades, he dismantled his own Tractatus position and developed a completely different approach to language. The Philosophical Investigations (1953, posthumous) is the central document. It is written in a distinctive style: numbered remarks, thought experiments, dialogues, and questions — never a systematic treatise. The style is intentional: traditional philosophy's demand for systematic theory is itself what needs to be dissolved.

metadata.title: Late Wittgenstein: Language Games and Meaning as Use

sections.text: The core reversal: where the Tractatus sought the hidden logical structure beneath language, the Investigations insists there is no such hidden structure. Language is what it appears to be — a collection of overlapping practices, none of which is the "true" essence of language.

metadata.title: Late Wittgenstein: Language Games and Meaning as Use

sections.text:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    TRACTATUS VS INVESTIGATIONS                        |
|                                                                       |
|  TRACTATUS (1921)                INVESTIGATIONS (1953)                |
|  -----------------               ------------------                   |
|  Language has ONE function:      Language has MANY functions:         |
|  picturing atomic facts          describing, questioning,             |
|                                  commanding, joking, greeting,        |
|                                  performing, praying...               |
|                                                                       |
|  Words get meaning by            Words get meaning by USE             |
|  NAMING objects                  in language games                    |
|                                                                       |
|  Meaning = the named object      Meaning = how the word is used       |
|                                                                       |
|  All propositions have           Different "regions" of language      |
|  the same LOGICAL FORM           have different grammars              |
|                                                                       |
|  Language mirrors                Language = diverse, embedded in      |
|  logical structure               forms of life (Lebensform)           |
|                                                                       |
|  Philosophy = logical analysis   Philosophy = therapeutic:            |
|               of language forms  dissolves confusions caused by       |
|                                  language's surface grammar           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
